issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Milkable.messageOnMilk() should return a String (and the textual requirements show it must return messages like "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). In the solution repository, Milkable.messageOnMilk() is declared to return boolean and the Goat and Seal implementations print the message and return true. This return-type mismatch (String vs boolean) contradicts the specification and will confuse students and tests expecting a String result.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable API with the problem specification: change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String. Update Goat and Seal to return the message string (e.g. "Goat Buttinsky is milked") instead of printing and returning boolean. Ensure callers (e.g. Main and singSong logic) print the returned String. Alternatively, if boolean is intended, update the problem statement and UML to specify a boolean return and adjust the textual requirements accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and instructions) and the template Main usage expect Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return a String with the text "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". However, the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return a boolean and its implementations (Seal, Goat) print the message and return true. This changes the method signature and behavior across artifacts, creating a mapping confusion for students (they expect a String-returning method with the specified message but the solution uses a boolean-returning method and side-effect printing).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable API and its implementations with the problem statement: change the interface signature to 'String messageOnMilk();' and modify Seal and Goat to return the string "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (do not print inside the method). Update any call sites accordingly.
